https://www.quartettoloco.com/.title: Quartetto Loco
https://www.quartettoloco.com/.description:
There is an imaginary place called Loco. Loco is not just a name for a place; it's a word for at least a dozen places: a village in the mountains, a quiet river, a swaying train, a laughing and crying cloud, a fond craziness, a word in a foreign dialect, an undiscovered irrational number, a nighttime banquet, a walk in the snow, a global embrace, a ripening fruit, and much more. People travel to Loco to momentarily forget where they come from and where they wish to go.

Loco comes into being when Quartetto Loco plays. Their music is both crazy and normal, dissonant yet harmonious, familiar and foreign. It emerges from the flickering between the knowledge of one's roots and the letting go of those roots. It's the freedom of forgetting and the richness of remembering. This first EP, with seven pieces, offers a glimpse into the musical place we call Loco. From free improvisation to twisted natural yodeling, from meditative original compositions to an individual interpretation of a short piece by Anton Webern, it is a journey through this imaginary landscape.

https://simonebottasso.bandcamp.com/albu.title: a dozen words for six, by Quartetto Loco
https://simonebottasso.bandcamp.com/albu.description:
This second EP, with six pieces, continues the exploration of the musical place we call Loco. From groovy original compositions to arrangements of music by Ursula Mamlok and Arnold Schönberg, from ethereal fugues to catalan Jota inspired tunes, it's a curious journey through this imaginary landscape.
The EP is titled “a dozen words for six” because, just as Loco is not just a word for one place but for at least a dozen, this EP is also “a dozen words for six”.

https://youtu.be/O2SjgTYsYvQ.title: Il Cielo di Pietra • Full performance @ De Roode Bioscoop (Amsterdam)
https://youtu.be/O2SjgTYsYvQ.author: Duo Bottasso
https://youtu.be/O2SjgTYsYvQ.description:
Il Cielo di Pietra is a live cinema performance in tribute to the seventh art: music and images meet and react to each other in an immersive and multidisciplinary show. The visual materials, from the archive of the Eye Film Museum in Amsterdam, were chosen from works by G. Melies, S. de Chomon and J.C. Mol. In homage to these pioneers of cinematic experimentation of the early twentieth century, videos are processed according to contemporary aesthetics through animation and visual processing. 
Thanks to the most modern multimedia technologies, the original music - performed live as in the first cinemas - influences and interacts with the projected fragments: sometimes the video fragments are projected starting from the played notes, other times the songs accompany a succession of images. The result is an audiovisual performance that manages to get the audience excited and involved, as happened on the occasion of the first film screening of the Lumiere Brothers when, according to legend, some spectators escaped from the room afraid of being overwhelmed by the train arriving on the screen.

Tenor Violin: Nicolò Bottasso 
Carillon; Richard de Waardt
Composition: Simone Bottasso 
Video & edit: Sid Duit

MUSICA DEI LUOGHI is a composition for carillon, organetto, and violin—three instruments that, perhaps because of their deep connection to rituals, always unlock vivid memories of places of celebration and contemplation.

It stems from a reflection on how cultures organize their own sonic expressions into forms in which they recognize themselves and which, afterwards, they might call classical or traditional.

It is also a tribute to those sonic languages which, once deeply rooted and widely shared within a community, are—sometimes too quickly—labeled by pairing a place name with “music.”

In composing it, Simone Bottasso was inspired by some melodies contained in the Groot Rotterdams Songbook, and he played with the rules and aesthetics—often rigorous—of classical and popular musical styles.

Neighbors

September 3rd 2025,
Start time: 20.00u

The trio features Simone Bottasso (organetto, composer, improviser) blending traditional and contemporary European music with dynamic stage presence; Reza Mirjalali (voice, Persian tar), combining classical Persian music inherited from his father Sharam with a modern twist; and Nicolò Bottasso on the violin and tenor violin. Neighbors has performed at major international festivals (Music Meeting, Etétrad, De Doelen, Musicamorfosi), contributed to the soundtrack of Biserta - Storia a Spirale (Cosenude Media Projects), and collaborated with the New Rotterdam Jazz Orchestra. 

In today’s fragile world, we believe music and art can transcend barriers and bring unity. Neighbors bridges East and West, creating “neighborly” relationships through shared cultural values. Traditional songs from the Italian Alps meet the Persian classical tradition of Radif and the rhythms of Indian tablas, blending improvisation and new compositions for a unique musical experience.

https://pietratonale.bandcamp.com/album/.title: Il Gioco della Campana, by Pietra Tonale
https://pietratonale.bandcamp.com/album/.description:
Il Gioco della Campana is inspired by Cortazar's Rayuela its structure is based on the non linear formal structure of the book.
As in Cortazar's novel, the composition is divided into three parts: the first two, Dall'altra parte (1-2) and Da questo parte (3), have a narrative contribution, while the third part, Da altre parti, is composed of micro movements including fragments of melodies from the pieces of the first two parts , extracts of bass lines, grooves, new melodies and short independent pieces which have the function, as in the novel, of abstracting from the dramaturgical line or integrating the narration or even bringing new thematic and harmonic elements to the attention of the listener.
In Cortazar's work, the reader can decide the order in which to read the chapters of the book, giving his own perspective to the author's writing, so in "Gioco Della Campana" the reader decides his interpretation by creating a new general structure using the musical chapters present in the composition. The work was written thinking of the ensemble of the Pietra Tonale Orchestra of Turin, the orchestra, which is also a collective, is composed of about twenty elements.
Il Gioco Della Campana was recorded on 27 and 28 September 2021 at the G. Verdi Conservatory in Turin, performed by Pietra Tonale Orchestra.

https://simonebottasso.bandcamp.com/albu.title: Il Canzoniere di Pasolini, by Linguamadre
https://simonebottasso.bandcamp.com/albu.description:
Pier Paolo Pasolini considered the Italian dialects to be the ultimate survival of something pure and uncontaminated that for him was to be protected. The lack of translation and the onomatopoeic values of some dialect words connect them to a deeper “truth”, making a strong bond between the word itself and the sound and feeling that the word evokes.
Linguamadre gives new sound and voice to the poems collected by Pasolini in his Canzoniere Italiano (Italian Songbook, 1955), using the modern aesthetics and techniques of today’s performers of oral-traditional music, creating original scores in which modern forms meld with lyrical and evocative atmospheres.
"Il Canzoniere di Pasolini" is the first live album by a band composed of four musicians coming from different regions of Italy and different musical fields. “Mother” is the keyword of their first work, seen both as the central figure that appears in many popular poems, and as the mother-tongue.
A breathtaking run among songs from the Earth, songs of invocation, songs of sweetness and alienation, songs of war and supplication that stand out against dreamlike chameleon soundscapes, rhythmic cavalcades and ticking ostinatos.

https://youtu.be/lyPspsqe2zU.title: LinguaMadre • Sa Limba
https://youtu.be/lyPspsqe2zU.author: Duo Bottasso
https://youtu.be/lyPspsqe2zU.description:
Scarno, essenziale, semplice. E' l'augurio per una nascitura in grembo raccolto da Pier Paolo Pasolini a Chiaramonti in provincia di Sassari, specchio di una saggezza popolare che contempla l'essenza nella sua nuda verità. 

Puri, concisi, sobri. Sono i timbri scelti per interpretare questo canto: la disarmante semplicità delle voci e delle linee strumentali, mai dissonanti e sempre complementari, sono una scelta consapevole e ragionata per valorizzare le peculiarità degli artisti e creare un intenso impasto di suoni. 

Nitido, minimale, limpido. E' la scelta del luogo e delle tecniche di ripresa per questo videoclip, mai eccessivo e sempre equilibrato ed essenziale. 

Eppure queste apparenti semplicità si trasformano in una danza travolgente, con un crescendo di dettagli indefiniti che rendono questo nuovo singolo di LinguaMadre potente ed evocativo. Composto a quattro mani da Davide Ambrogio e Simone Bottasso, è l'augurio che la creatura nel grembo possa un giorno danzare senza pregiudizi sulle note di una melodia tanto ancestrale quanto minimalista. Il nome della piccola? Ancora non lo sappiamo, ma confidiamo sia Arte.
